method: A Code 39 symbol is a start character, the data characters, an optional check character and a stop character, each drawn as nine elements - five bars and four spaces - of which exactly three are wide. Every element is one module (narrow) or three modules (wide), so a symbol is fifteen modules across, and a single one-module space separates one symbol from the next. The page draws those modules as black and white runs and wraps the whole barcode in ten-module quiet zones, the space a scanner needs at either end. The 43 characters of the standard set are the digits, the capital letters and - . space $ / + %, with values 0 to 42 in that published order, and the asterisk is the start and stop symbol - it is added automatically and refused in the data. When the check character is enabled, the values of the data characters are summed and reduced modulo 43, and the character at that value is inserted before the stop symbol. Lower case, control characters and the full-ASCII pairs Code 39 would need for them are not offered, so the page is not an extended Code 39 encoder, and the text is limited to 40 characters to keep a printed label readable. The pattern table and the check character are checked against the symbology, but a printed label still has to be test-scanned at the module width the label and scanner need. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
